items.action: Create harness_lib/bubble_memo.py, pure (no config reads at import time; the root is an argument). Anchors as constants: MEMO_SUFFIX, INDEX_HEADER, STATUS_OPEN, STATUS_DECIDED, DECISION_OPEN, DECISION_PREFIX, ENTRY_PREFIX, STUB. Functions: memo_name(pr); currently_bubbled(doc, pending) -> Bubbled(id, cls, reason) (bubbles in order, then pending pairs not already present; class from bubble_up, else the pending pair, else 'unclassified'); flagged_ids(doc, ids) and needs_chain; reviewer_model(flagged); scaffold_memo(doc, bubbled); add_missing(text, doc, bubbled) -> (text, added) that appends entries and index rows and never edits existing text; parse_index and entry_blocks; check_memo(text, bubbled, doc, root) -> (problems, notes) with the rules of spec Section 1 (check) and problem lines formatted '<ID>: <what>'; Facts (pydantic) with validate_facts(raw, issue, root) that refuses an empty field, a fix_effects count different from the issue's fix list, and any reference whose file or line is not on disk; apply_facts(text, facts) that replaces only the flagged entry's References, Current behavior, When, Chain, flow and Expected-behavior stubs. Entry layout: spec 'Memo format'; a reference is a backticked path:line or path:start-end; an expected-behavior line is '- (a) <fix text> -> <effect>'. Python 3.11, Optional/Union, functions under 50 lines, no first or second person in comments.

items.action: Create scripts/bubble_memo.py following plan.py's shape: sys.path insert of ../lib, argparse with --repo and subcommands, main(argv) returning 0 or 1, one 'problem: ...' line per defect on stderr, activate(load_config(project_root(...))) once. Commands per spec Section 1: scaffold --pr N (reads the newest <NNNN>_*.json for N from artifacts.reviews, the pending fixer bubbles through review_bubbles when a pr-review run exists and falls back to bubbles alone when it does not; creates or extends <artifacts.reviews>/PR_<N>_Bubbles.md; prints a 'scaffold [done]' line, the added and flagged ids and one investigator dispatch row per newly added flagged id; prints 'nothing currently bubbled' and writes no memo when the set is empty); init --pr N --id ID --role investigator and init --pr N --role reviewer (print the brief and save it under the agent scratch folder; git facts via read-only git, excerpts from the working tree, the exact record command); record --pr N [--id ID] --role investigator|reviewer (JSON on stdin; validate through the library, refuse off-disk references, write facts/<ID>.json or findings/<N>.json, print the fenced return block with SIGNAL: DONE); apply --pr N; check --pr N (exit 1 with '<ID>: <what>' problem lines, 'note:' lines never fail; when clean print 'check [ok]' and the reviewer dispatch row with model from reviewer_model and a 'Memo: <abs path>' prompt line). Dispatch rows: agent=<type> model=<m>, then PR, ISSUE (investigator), FILES (comma-separated), CONTEXT (one line, name plus class plus reason) and an optional Developer guidance line. The prompt never carries RUN_ID or AGENT_ID header lines.

items.title: Agents: investigator and reviewer, and the usage-log list
items.action: Create agents/bubble-memo-investigator.md and agents/bubble-memo-reviewer.md in pr-reviewer's shape: frontmatter name equal to the file stem, tools 'Read, Grep, Glob, Bash', a fallback model (investigator opus, reviewer sonnet; the dispatcher passes the model each printed row names), examples. Body: the prompt is a few header lines (PR, ISSUE, FILES, CONTEXT, Memo for the reviewer, optional Developer guidance); the first action is the `init` call exactly as the prompt's launcher writes it (sh hpy bubble_memo.py init ...); work from its output; run `record` exactly once; reply with the printed block verbatim and nothing else; 'Never write files', 'Read-only git' (show, diff, log, status, merge-base, rev-parse, ls-files, grep only), one command per Bash call, stop with 'problem:' lines when init fails or record fails three times. Investigator: trace the issue through the cited code and report current behavior, when it triggers, chain, flow, opened references and one effect per fix option; it does not write a recommendation or memo prose. Reviewer: accuracy (references exist and say what the entry claims, claims agree with the code, expected behavior follows from each fix, nothing contradicts the review JSON) and clarity and simplicity (ordinary words, one claim per bullet, nothing repeated, the recommendation stated once); findings are {id, kind, what, suggested}. Add both names to DEFINED_AGENTS in pr-review-watch's contract.ts in sorted order (they sort before harness:messenger).
